findings.title: Legacy-path ex.onAbort registration aborts an already-upgraded WebSocket response mid-session and writes a spurious 'GET /ws 200 aborted' access line

location.line_range: 286-288 (interaction with 303-315 onDone access line and DefaultResponse.upgraded():923-947)

findings.description: HttpExchange.webSocket returns only after the connection closed, and DefaultResponse stays NEW for the whole session because upgraded() runs only after webSocket returns. With the new registration, an adapter-reported abort during an open session (TinyHttpdAdapter.stop aborts every tracked exchange; an upgraded TinyHttpdExchange is tracked and not finished during the session) now calls res.abort(null) while the session is still running: the response goes NEW->ABORTED, ex.abort() is called re-entrantly from inside the adapter's abort callback, onDone fires before the session ended, and because upgraded101 stays false the onDone hook writes a request access line with the never-sent status 200 and 'aborted', duplicating the session's 'GET /ws 101' line for the same rid. Before this change the same scenario ended via upgraded() (upgraded101=true, finish failure -> ABORTED, listeners once) with exactly one request line. Listener count (1) is unchanged; the regression is the extra, wrong access line and the response being terminated while the upgraded session still owns the exchange.
findings.suggested_fix: Scope the legacy registration to the pre-101 window: e.g. make the registered callback skip once the upgrade began (a flag set right before upgrades.run / ex.webSocket, or a DefaultResponse 'upgrading' state that abort() from the exchange hook leaves for upgraded() to resolve), or have res.abort from the exchange hook mark upgraded101 when the 101 was already written. Add a regression test like the proof above asserting one 'GET /ws' request line when the exchange reports an abort after onOpen.

clean_code.principle: Consistency / one way to do one thing in a test class
clean_code.observation: The new test intercepts HttpExchange.onAbort with a java.lang.reflect.Proxy around RecordingExchange, while the same class already has a hand-written delegating exchange (SilentExchange) for the SPI-default case; two different interception mechanisms for the same seam. A small reusable helper (e.g. an abort-reporting wrapper in testFixtures) would serve both. Not a defect; the test itself is sound (no sleeps, does not mock DefaultResponse/Dispatcher, fails without the fix, asserts once-per-listener and ABORTED and no upgrade).
